gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured scan time for a real car part: in a King Saud University lab study (Applied Sciences, 2018) a white-light handheld scanner (Creaform Go!SCAN) scanned a car door in 2.66 min against 10.36 min for a laser handheld (Creaform VIUscan), at the cost of accuracy (0.1995 mm vs 0.1285 mm RMS deviation).
standout_why: Compared against 3D Wonders' 'Best 3D Scanner for Automotive Inspection in 2026' (top result in two chats), which gives only maker specs plus an unattributed '5-15 minutes' body-panel capture time naming no scanner or tester, and against the three ChatGPT answers, which list only maker points-per-second and field-of-view figures (dim3nsions/Shining 3D brochures, Rev1, SKYLAB3D, SCANOLOGY PDFs, EMS3D, Print3DIndex, Polyrix) and say outright that no independently measured completion times exist. None of them has a timed car-part scan by a named lab or reviewer. The study is new to the result set but uses 2018-era Creaform hardware, not the current candidates, so it informs the speed-vs-accuracy trade-off rather than ranking today's models.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's own caveat with a number: on a car door, the area-capture (white/blue structured-light) scanner finished about 3.9x faster than the laser-line scanner but was less accurate, so 'fastest for a big car part' depends on the accuracy needed. For shape capture (1-2 mm) a structured-light or IR large-area mode is the faster pick; for 0.1 mm fitment work a laser tracker system (Trak Nova, KSCAN-X, HandySCAN MAX) costs scan time. It does not pick between the current laser trackers, for which no named timed test of a car part exists.

findings.label: Measured scan time, automotive car door
findings.source_title: Evaluation of Handheld Scanners for Automotive Applications (Ameen, Al-Ahmari, Mian; King Saud University; Applied Sciences 8(2):217, published 2018-01-31)
findings.note: Lab study at King Saud University's Advanced Manufacturing Institute; free-form car door (dimensions not given); optimized settings 1.5 mm resolution; full factorial design (18 runs) plus validation with 10 users per scanner. findings.product: SHINING 3D FreeScan UE Pro (predecessor of UE Nova)
findings.label: Aniwaa timed large-object scan

findings.source_title: FreeScan UE Pro review: cost-effective metrology-grade 3D scanner that delivers (Aniwaa, Pierre-Antoine Arrighi, 2022-10-18)
findings.note: Cross-lines laser mode with markers 15-25 cm apart plus photogrammetry; Arrighi says marker placement and removal 'takes the longest' but did not time it. findings.label: Aniwaa timed scan of a >1 m object, laser vs infrared mode
findings.value: about 10 min laser (0.2 mm) vs about 5 min invisible-light large-object mode
findings.source_title: SHINING 3D FreeScan Combo review: small, but mighty? (Aniwaa, Pierre-Antoine Arrighi, 2023-12-19)
findings.note: Object: heater and pipes on a stone wall (>1 m); IR mode used marker alignment; Arrighi called it 'significantly faster than when using the laser mode'. Same direction as the King Saud result: area capture beats laser lines on time.

findings.label: Vendor-run shop-floor benchmark, total inspection time on an 800 x 1000 x 1000 mm mold
findings.value: 45 min vs 294 min for an unnamed blue-light scanner
findings.source_title: Results Revealed and Facts Exposed: Benchmarking Two 3D Scanning Metrology Solutions to Save Inspection Time (Creaform blog, 2024-04-29)
findings.note: Measured by Creaform with engineers at an unnamed automotive mold company, so not independent. Steps: setup/prep 5 vs 84 min, scan + post-processing 30 vs 180 min, cleaning 10 vs 30 min. Shows that prep (spray, targets) can outweigh capture speed; it reverses the King Saud ranking because the blue-light unit needed spray and more setup on a shiny part.
